title: Endpoint DLP: what Microsoft Purview enforces on onboarded devices
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports its controls, licensing and qualified descriptions of classification, offline enforcement and just-in-time protection. Minor corrections should restore two policy-wizard headings, cite the Power Platform comparison and acknowledge conflicting macOS version wording in the service description.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP extends Microsoft Purview DLP monitoring and protection to sensitive files on onboarded devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) is part of the Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) suite of features you can use to discover and protect sensitive items across Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP supports Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) extends the activity monitoring and protection capabilities of DLP to Windows 10/11, macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices, and Windows certain server versions.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Endpoint DLP support for the three latest released major macOS versions.
claims.quote: macOS (the three latest released major versions)
claims.fix: After the platform-support sentence, add: 'The Purview service description instead lists macOS Catalina 10.15 and higher.' That conflicting wording appears at https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-data-loss-prevention-endpoint-data-loss-protection-dlp.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP supports certain Windows Server versions.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP allows you to onboard devices running Windows Server 2019 and later versions.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP is distinct from Power Platform data policies.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention to sources for the comparison with Power Platform data policies; retain the existing Endpoint DLP overview citation for device-file protection.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified on creation or modification
claims.claim: On Windows 10/11 and macOS, creating a file triggers a full scan for sensitive information types and labels.
claims.quote: Creation or Modification: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified on creation or modification
claims.claim: On Windows 10/11 and macOS, modifying a file triggers a full scan for sensitive information types and labels.
claims.quote: Creation or Modification: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified on creation or modification
claims.claim: Reading an already classified file triggers policy re-evaluation if policies, rules or sensitive information types changed.
claims.quote: When an already classified file is read, Endpoint DLP checks for any changes to the policies, rules, or SITs. If there is a change in the DLP configuration, it re-evaluates the policies and rules, but it will not re-extract the text.

claims.where: What it is: Policies are scoped by user and device; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: For a Devices-location policy to be enforced, both the user and device must be in scope.
claims.quote: For a DLP policy to be enforced on an endpoint, both the user and the device must be included in the policy scope.

claims.where: What it is: Policies are scoped by user and device
claims.claim: A device needs access to all endpoint DLP policies because it can support multiple users with different policies.
claims.quote: A device can support multiple user accounts. Because endpoint policies are scoped to users, different users of the device may have different policies scoped to them. Therefore, the device must have access to all endpoint DLP policies in order to evaluate items.

claims.where: What it is: Endpoint settings; controls[1].governs; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Centrally configured endpoint settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can audit or restrict copying sensitive files to USB removable devices.
claims.quote: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to USB removable media.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can audit or restrict copying sensitive files to network shares.
claims.quote: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to any network share, including redirected USB devices that are displayed as network shares on an Azure Virtual Desktop with Windows 365.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can audit or restrict printing sensitive files.
claims.quote: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the printing of protected files from an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can audit or restrict copying protected file content to the clipboard.
claims.quote: When a user attempts to copy content from a protected file, you can block, block with override, or audit the copying of protected files to a clipboard on an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP can audit or restrict uploading protected files to restricted cloud service domains.
claims.quote: You can block, warn, or audit when protected files can be uploaded or prevented from being uploaded to cloud services based on the allow/unallowed domains list in Data loss prevention settings.

claims.claim: The copy-or-move-using-RDP activity is not supported on macOS.
claims.quote: | Copy or move using RDP | Detects when a user attempts to copy an item to a remote desktop session. | Supported | Supported | Not supported | Auditable and restrictable |

claims.where: What it is: Just-in-time protection; controls[4].governs
claims.claim: JIT protection can block egress on monitored unevaluated or stale files while policy evaluation completes.
claims.quote: After you enable JIT, Endpoint DLP blocks the activity and generates an event in activity explorer for every JIT candidate file.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on whether the user is in scope.
claims.quote: The user is in the scope of JIT.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on the DLP actions configured for the egress activity.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies exist that block or block with override for the egress activity.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on whether the egress destination is allowed.
claims.quote: The egress activity isn't to an allowed location. For example, an allowed printer, USB device, URL, or network share.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on pause-and-resume support.
claims.quote: The egress activity doesn't support JIT pause and resume.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP enforcement happens on the device.
claims.quote: When a Windows endpoint device is offline, existing policies continue to be enforced on existing files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices
claims.claim: An offline Windows endpoint continues enforcing existing policies on existing files.
claims.quote: When a Windows endpoint device is offline, existing policies continue to be enforced on existing files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices
claims.claim: Policy changes are not pushed to a Windows endpoint while it is offline.
claims.quote: Policies that are updated while a device is offline won't be pushed to that device. Similarly, such policies won't be enforced on that device, until the device is back online.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices
claims.claim: Policy changes reach the Windows endpoint after it reconnects.
claims.quote: If a new policy is created on the server, or an existing policy is modified, those changes are updated on the device once it reconnects to the internet.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices
claims.claim: Microsoft states that the described offline functionality is not supported on macOS endpoints.
claims.quote: This functionality isn't supported on macOS endpoint devices.

claims.claim: Onboarded devices audit activity on Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF and CSV files by default even if no policy targets them.
claims.quote: If the Always audit file activity for devices setting is on, activities on any Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and .csv files are always audited, even if the device isn't targeted by any policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Always audit file activity for devices can be turned off to limit auditing to policy-targeted devices.
claims.quote: By default, when you onboard devices, the system automatically audits activity for Office, PDF, and CSV files. You can review this activity in activity explorer. Turn off this feature if you want to audit this activity only when onboarded devices are included in an active policy.

claims.claim: Audited device activity can appear in Activity explorer before any device policy is configured.
claims.quote: Once a device is onboarded, information about audited activities flows into Activity explorer even before you configure and deploy any DLP policies that have devices as a location.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP is not enabled for Windows servers when they are initially onboarded.
claims.quote: By default, Endpoint DLP isn't enabled for Windows servers when they're initially onboarded.

claims.quote: If a policy is scoped to devices where the signed-in users do not meet the required criteria, ensure those users or devices or both are explicitly excluded from the policy. Failure to do so may lead to unintended policy enforcement behavior.

claims.quote: If you set a bandwidth usage limit and that usage limit is exceeded, DLP stops sending the user content to the cloud.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced classification has a bandwidth limit

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced classification has a bandwidth limit
claims.claim: Cloud classification communication resumes when cumulative bandwidth use drops below the limit.
claims.quote: When the cumulative bandwidth usage drops below the rolling 24-hour limit, communication with the cloud services resumes.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced classification has a bandwidth limit

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-DlpCompliancePolicy -EndpointDlpLocation <MultiValuedProperty> for selecting included user accounts by name, email or All, rather than selecting device groups.
